# Engage: The Investigative Phenomenon

::: {.engage-box}
## 🌍 Storm Tracks: 2018–2020

<div style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; margin: 20px 0; text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);">
Maps from 2018–2020 show that blizzards and hurricanes exhibit clear patterns in where they start and the direction they travel.
</div>

### 🤔 Key Observations:
- 🌀 Hurricanes form over **warm tropical oceans** and move **westward, then curve northeast**
- 🌨️ Blizzards track along the **East Coast**, moving from **southwest to northeast**
- 🗺️ Neither storm type occurs **randomly** — they follow **predictable pathways**

**Driving Question:** Why do severe storms follow specific paths, and what could cause those paths to change?
:::

::: {.student-task}
### 📝 Pattern Spotting

Look at the storm track maps below. Before we explain the science, write down:

1. What **geographic patterns** do you notice in storm tracks?
2. What **direction** do most storms move in the mid-latitudes?
3. Why do you think hurricanes start near the equator but blizzards start in the mid-latitudes?
:::

# Explore: Mapping Storm Trajectories

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔬 Investigation: Where Do Storms Go?

Let's visualize real storm trajectory patterns and look for the underlying cause of these paths.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot = require("@observablehq/plot")
d3 = require("d3@7")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof stormTypeMap = Inputs.radio(
  ["Atlantic Hurricanes", "Northeast Blizzards", "Both"],
  {label: "Show storm tracks:", value: "Both"}
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const topojson = await require("topojson-client@3");
  const world = await fetch("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2/land-50m.json").then(r => r.json());
  const land = topojson.feature(world, world.objects.land);

  // Hurricane tracks [lon, lat] — classic Atlantic recurvature patterns
  const hurricaneTracksData = [
    [[-45,13],[-52,16],[-58,19],[-64,22],[-69,26],[-72,30],[-72,35],[-70,39],[-65,43]],
    [[-84,23],[-81,26],[-78,29],[-74,32],[-71,36],[-69,41],[-65,46]],
    [[-75,16],[-79,20],[-80,24],[-77,28],[-74,33],[-70,38],[-66,43]]
  ];

  // Nor'easter tracks [lon, lat] — forming in Gulf/SE states, tracking up the East Coast
  const blizzardTracksData = [
    [[-89,30],[-85,33],[-80,36],[-76,39],[-73,41],[-70,44],[-67,48],[-62,52]],
    [[-91,32],[-87,35],[-83,38],[-78,40],[-75,42],[-72,45],[-68,50]],
    [[-87,31],[-83,34],[-79,37],[-75,39],[-72,42],[-69,46],[-65,51]]
  ];

  const nycDot = [{lon: -74, lat: 40.7}];

  const marks = [
    Plot.geo({type:"Sphere"}, {fill:"#1b263b"}),
    Plot.geo(land, {fill:"#2d5016", stroke:"#4caf50", strokeWidth:0.5}),
    Plot.dot(nycDot, {x:"lon", y:"lat", r:5, fill:"#f44336", stroke:"white", strokeWidth:1.5}),
    Plot.text(nycDot, {x:"lon", y:"lat", text:["NYC"], fill:"#f44336", fontWeight:"bold", fontSize:11, dx:8})
  ];

  if (stormTypeMap === "Atlantic Hurricanes" || stormTypeMap === "Both") {
    const colors = ["#e74c3c","#c0392b","#e67e22"];
    hurricaneTracksData.forEach((pts, i) => {
      marks.push(Plot.line(pts, {x:d=>d[0], y:d=>d[1], stroke:colors[i], strokeWidth:2.5, curve:"catmull-rom", strokeDasharray:"8,3"}));
      marks.push(Plot.dot([pts[0]], {x:d=>d[0], y:d=>d[1], r:5, fill:colors[i]}));
      marks.push(Plot.text([pts[pts.length-1]], {x:d=>d[0], y:d=>d[1], text:["🌀"], fontSize:16}));
    });
  }

  if (stormTypeMap === "Northeast Blizzards" || stormTypeMap === "Both") {
    const bcolors = ["#3498db","#2980b9","#1abc9c"];
    blizzardTracksData.forEach((pts, i) => {
      marks.push(Plot.line(pts, {x:d=>d[0], y:d=>d[1], stroke:bcolors[i], strokeWidth:2.5, curve:"catmull-rom"}));
      marks.push(Plot.dot([pts[0]], {x:d=>d[0], y:d=>d[1], r:5, fill:bcolors[i]}));
      marks.push(Plot.text([pts[pts.length-1]], {x:d=>d[0], y:d=>d[1], text:["🌨️"], fontSize:16}));
    });
  }

  return Plot.plot({
    title: "Storm Track Patterns — Atlantic Hurricanes & Northeast Blizzards",
    subtitle: "Both storm types curve SW → NE across the mid-latitudes",
    width: 750,
    height: 480,
    projection: {
      type: "equirectangular",
      domain: {type:"MultiPoint", coordinates:[[-105,5],[-35,68]]}
    },
    style: {background:"#1b263b", color:"#eee", fontSize:"12px"},
    marks
  });
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Key Observation

Despite forming in very different locations and for very different reasons, both hurricanes (once they curve north) and blizzards travel in the **same general direction**: from **southwest to northeast** across the mid-latitudes.

This is NOT a coincidence. Something is **steering** these storms.
:::

# Explain: The Global Wind Engine

::: {.explain-box}
## 🌬️ Why Does the Wind Blow the Way It Does?

To understand storm paths, we need to understand the global circulation of the atmosphere — the "engine" that steers weather systems around the planet.
:::

## Uneven Solar Heating: The Root Cause

The Sun doesn't heat Earth evenly. The equator receives far more solar energy per unit area than the poles because of the angle at which sunlight hits the surface.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const width = 750;
  const height = 380;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);

  svg.append("rect").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("fill", "#1a1a2e").attr("rx", 10);

  // Earth (circle)
  const cx = 375, cy = 200, r = 140;
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", r).attr("fill", "#2980b9");

  // Latitude bands
  const bands = [
    {y1: -1, y2: -0.5, label: "60-90°N", color: "#74b9ff", energy: "Low"},
    {y1: -0.5, y2: 0, label: "30-60°N", color: "#a29bfe", energy: "Medium"},
    {y1: 0, y2: 0.5, label: "0-30°N", color: "#fdcb6e", energy: "High"},
    {y1: 0.5, y2: 1, label: "0-30°S", color: "#fdcb6e", energy: "High"}
  ];

  bands.forEach(b => {
    const y1 = cy - b.y1 * r;
    const y2 = cy - b.y2 * r;
    const x1 = cx - Math.sqrt(r*r - (cy-y1)*(cy-y1)) || cx;
    const x2 = cx + Math.sqrt(r*r - (cy-y1)*(cy-y1)) || cx;
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", x1).attr("y1", y1).attr("x2", x2).attr("y2", y1)
      .attr("stroke", b.color).attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");
  });

  // Sun rays
  const sunX = 100;
  const rays = [
    {y: cy - 100, angle: 30, label: "Spread out → less energy/area", color: "#74b9ff"},
    {y: cy, angle: 0, label: "Direct → maximum energy/area", color: "#f39c12"},
    {y: cy + 80, angle: -20, label: "Spread out → less energy/area", color: "#74b9ff"}
  ];

  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", 50).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", 30).attr("fill", "#f39c12");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 50).attr("y", cy + 5).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 20).text("☀️");

  rays.forEach(ray => {
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", 90).attr("y1", ray.y).attr("x2", cx - r + 20).attr("y2", ray.y + Math.tan(ray.angle * Math.PI/180) * 200)
      .attr("stroke", ray.color).attr("stroke-width", 2);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + r + 20).attr("y", ray.y + 5).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", ray.color).text(ray.label);
  });

  // Energy bar chart on right
  const barData = [{lat: "Equator", energy: 100}, {lat: "30°", energy: 75}, {lat: "60°", energy: 40}, {lat: "90°", energy: 15}];
  const barX = 620;
  barData.forEach((d, i) => {
    const barW = d.energy * 0.8;
    const barY = 100 + i * 55;
    svg.append("rect").attr("x", barX).attr("y", barY).attr("width", barW).attr("height", 30)
      .attr("fill", d.energy > 60 ? "#f39c12" : "#74b9ff").attr("rx", 4);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", barX - 5).attr("y", barY + 20).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "white").text(d.lat);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", barX + barW + 5).attr("y", barY + 20).attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#dfe6e9").text(`${d.energy}%`);
  });

  svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 370).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 14).attr("fill", "#dfe6e9").attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text("Uneven heating creates a temperature gradient from equator to poles → drives atmospheric circulation");

  return svg.node();
}
```

## Convection Cells: Nature's Heat Redistributors

This uneven heating drives enormous **convection cells** in the atmosphere — rising warm air near the equator and sinking cool air at higher latitudes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const width = 750;
  const height = 500;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);

  svg.append("rect").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("fill", "#f0f4ff").attr("rx", 10);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 30).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 20).attr("font-weight", "bold").text("Global Atmospheric Circulation Cells");

  // Earth surface line
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", 50).attr("y1", 400).attr("x2", 700).attr("y2", 400).attr("stroke", "#2d3436").attr("stroke-width", 3);

  // Latitude labels
  const lats = [{x: 50, label: "90°N"}, {x: 158, label: "60°N"}, {x: 267, label: "30°N"}, {x: 375, label: "0° (Equator)"}, {x: 483, label: "30°S"}, {x: 592, label: "60°S"}, {x: 700, label: "90°S"}];
  lats.forEach(l => {
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", l.x).attr("y1", 395).attr("x2", l.x).attr("y2", 405).attr("stroke", "#2d3436").attr("stroke-width", 2);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", l.x).attr("y", 420).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).text(l.label);
  });

  // Hadley Cells (equator to 30°)
  const drawCell = (x1, x2, y1, y2, color, name, direction) => {
    svg.append("rect").attr("x", Math.min(x1,x2)).attr("y", y2).attr("width", Math.abs(x2-x1)).attr("height", y1-y2)
      .attr("fill", color).attr("opacity", 0.15).attr("rx", 5);
    // Circulation arrows
    const midX = (x1+x2)/2;
    const midY = (y1+y2)/2;
    if (direction === "cw") {
      svg.append("path").attr("d", `M ${x1+10},${y1-10} L ${x1+10},${y2+10} L ${x2-10},${y2+10} L ${x2-10},${y1-10}`)
        .attr("stroke", color).attr("stroke-width", 2.5).attr("fill", "none").attr("marker-end", `url(#arrow-${name})`);
    } else {
      svg.append("path").attr("d", `M ${x2-10},${y1-10} L ${x2-10},${y2+10} L ${x1+10},${y2+10} L ${x1+10},${y1-10}`)
        .attr("stroke", color).attr("stroke-width", 2.5).attr("fill", "none").attr("marker-end", `url(#arrow-${name})`);
    }
    svg.append("text").attr("x", midX).attr("y", midY).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 13).attr("font-weight", "bold").attr("fill", color).text(name);

    const defs = svg.select("defs").empty() ? svg.append("defs") : svg.select("defs");
    defs.append("marker").attr("id", `arrow-${name}`).attr("viewBox", "0 0 10 10").attr("refX", 5).attr("refY", 5)
      .attr("markerWidth", 6).attr("markerHeight", 6).attr("orient", "auto-start-reverse")
      .append("path").attr("d", "M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z").attr("fill", color);
  };

  // Polar Cell (90-60°N)
  drawCell(50, 158, 390, 200, "#3498db", "Polar", "cw");
  // Ferrel Cell (60-30°N)
  drawCell(158, 267, 390, 150, "#9b59b6", "Ferrel", "ccw");
  // Hadley Cell (30-0°N)
  drawCell(267, 375, 390, 100, "#e74c3c", "Hadley", "cw");
  // Hadley Cell (0-30°S)
  drawCell(375, 483, 390, 100, "#e74c3c", "Hadley", "ccw");
  // Ferrel Cell (30-60°S)
  drawCell(483, 592, 390, 150, "#9b59b6", "Ferrel", "cw");
  // Polar Cell (60-90°S)
  drawCell(592, 700, 390, 200, "#3498db", "Polar", "ccw");

  // Surface wind labels
  const winds = [
    {x: 104, y: 440, text: "Polar Easterlies", arrow: "←"},
    {x: 212, y: 440, text: "Westerlies", arrow: "→"},
    {x: 321, y: 440, text: "Trade Winds (NE)", arrow: "←"},
    {x: 429, y: 440, text: "Trade Winds (SE)", arrow: "→"},
    {x: 537, y: 440, text: "Westerlies", arrow: "←"},
    {x: 646, y: 440, text: "Polar Easterlies", arrow: "→"}
  ];

  winds.forEach(w => {
    svg.append("text").attr("x", w.x).attr("y", w.y).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#2d3436").text(w.text);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", w.x).attr("y", w.y + 18).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 18).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text(w.arrow);
  });

  // Rising/sinking labels
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 85).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text("↑ Rising (ITCZ)");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 267).attr("y", 85).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#e67e22").text("↓ Sinking");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 483).attr("y", 85).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#e67e22").text("↓ Sinking");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 158).attr("y", 140).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#3498db").text("↑ Rising");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 592).attr("y", 140).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#3498db").text("↑ Rising");

  // Jet stream markers
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 140).attr("y", 170).attr("width", 36).attr("height", 20).attr("fill", "#f1c40f").attr("rx", 4);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 158).attr("y", 185).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 10).attr("font-weight", "bold").text("JET");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 249).attr("y", 125).attr("width", 36).attr("height", 20).attr("fill", "#f1c40f").attr("rx", 4);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 267).attr("y", 140).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 10).attr("font-weight", "bold").text("JET");

  svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 490).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#636e72")
    .text("NYC sits in the WESTERLIES zone → storms are steered from west/southwest to east/northeast");

  return svg.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Key Concept: Three Circulation Cells

| Cell | Latitude | Surface Winds | Key Feature |
|------|----------|---------------|-------------|
| **Hadley** | 0°–30° | Trade Winds (NE in NH) | Rising air at equator → heavy rain; sinking at 30° → deserts |
| **Ferrel** | 30°–60° | **Westerlies** | Driven by Hadley & Polar cells; steers mid-latitude weather from W→E |
| **Polar** | 60°–90° | Polar Easterlies | Cold, dry air sinking at poles |

**NYC is at ~41°N — right in the Ferrel Cell's westerlies.** This is why storms affecting our city generally move from southwest to northeast!
:::

## The Coriolis Effect: Why Winds Curve

If Earth didn't rotate, winds would blow straight from high to low pressure. But Earth **does** rotate, and this deflects moving air:

- **Northern Hemisphere:** winds curve to the **RIGHT**
- **Southern Hemisphere:** winds curve to the **LEFT**

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
{
  const width = 400;
  const height = 400;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);

  // Earth from above (North Pole view)
  const cx = 200, cy = 200, r = 160;
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", r).attr("fill", "#e3f2fd").attr("stroke", "#1565c0").attr("stroke-width", 2);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx).attr("y", cy).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold").text("N. Pole (top view)");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx).attr("y", cy + 20).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 20).text("↺");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx).attr("y", cy + 40).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#636e72").text("Earth rotates CCW");

  if (!showCoriolis) {
    // Straight path (no Coriolis)
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", cx).attr("y1", cy - r + 20).attr("x2", cx).attr("y2", cy + r - 20)
      .attr("stroke", "#2ecc71").attr("stroke-width", 3).attr("marker-end", "url(#arrowGreen)");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + 15).attr("y", cy - 30).attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#2ecc71").text("Expected path");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + 15).attr("y", cy - 15).attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#2ecc71").text("(no rotation)");
  } else {
    // Curved path (with Coriolis)
    svg.append("path").attr("d", `M ${cx},${cy - r + 20} Q ${cx + 80},${cy} ${cx + 40},${cy + r - 40}`)
      .attr("stroke", "#e74c3c").attr("stroke-width", 3).attr("fill", "none").attr("marker-end", "url(#arrowRed)");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + 90).attr("y", cy - 10).attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text("Actual path");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + 90).attr("y", cy + 5).attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text("(deflected RIGHT)");
    // Ghost straight path
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", cx).attr("y1", cy - r + 20).attr("x2", cx).attr("y2", cy + r - 20)
      .attr("stroke", "#2ecc71").attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "5,3");
  }

  const defs = svg.append("defs");
  defs.append("marker").attr("id", "arrowGreen").attr("viewBox", "0 0 10 10").attr("refX", 5).attr("refY", 5)
    .attr("markerWidth", 6).attr("markerHeight", 6).attr("orient", "auto-start-reverse")
    .append("path").attr("d", "M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z").attr("fill", "#2ecc71");
  defs.append("marker").attr("id", "arrowRed").attr("viewBox", "0 0 10 10").attr("refX", 5).attr("refY", 5)
    .attr("markerWidth", 6).attr("markerHeight", 6).attr("orient", "auto-start-reverse")
    .append("path").attr("d", "M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z").attr("fill", "#e74c3c");

  return svg.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Key Concept: Coriolis Effect + Pressure Gradient = Surface Winds

- Without Coriolis: wind blows straight from H → L pressure
- With Coriolis (NH): wind is deflected **right** → curves clockwise around High pressure, counter-clockwise around Low pressure
- This is why tropical trade winds blow from the **northeast** (not straight south) and mid-latitude westerlies blow from the **southwest** (not straight north)
:::

## The Jet Stream: The Storm Highway

At the boundary between the Ferrel and Polar cells (~60°N, but it meanders), there is an extremely fast river of air flowing from west to east at high altitude: the **jet stream**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof jetStreamPattern = Inputs.radio(
  ["Normal Pattern", "Wavy Pattern (Blocking)", "Climate Change Projection"],
  {label: "Jet stream configuration:", value: "Normal Pattern"}
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const width = 750;
  const height = 350;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);

  svg.append("rect").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("fill", "#f0f4ff").attr("rx", 10);

  // US outline simplified
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 50).attr("y", 100).attr("width", 650).attr("height", 200).attr("fill", "#e8f5e9").attr("rx", 5);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 100).attr("y", 130).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#4caf50").text("🇨🇦 CANADA (cold air)");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 100).attr("y", 280).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#ef5350").text("🌴 SOUTH (warm air)");

  // Latitude reference
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 710).attr("y", 155).attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#999").text("50°N");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 710).attr("y", 205).attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#999").text("40°N");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 710).attr("y", 255).attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#999").text("30°N");

  if (jetStreamPattern === "Normal Pattern") {
    svg.append("path")
      .attr("d", "M 50,190 Q 200,170 350,195 Q 500,220 650,185 L 700,185")
      .attr("stroke", "#1565c0").attr("stroke-width", 5).attr("fill", "none");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 160).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold").attr("fill", "#1565c0")
      .text("Polar Jet Stream (~200 mph)");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 330).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 13)
      .text("Gentle waves → storms track steadily from west to east");
    // Storm riding the jet
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 400).attr("y", 205).attr("font-size", 20).text("🌀");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 430).attr("y", 210).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text("Storm steered by jet →");
  } else if (jetStreamPattern === "Wavy Pattern (Blocking)") {
    svg.append("path")
      .attr("d", "M 50,190 Q 130,130 210,220 Q 290,300 370,180 Q 450,100 530,240 Q 610,310 700,190")
      .attr("stroke", "#e74c3c").attr("stroke-width", 5).attr("fill", "none");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 80).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold").attr("fill", "#e74c3c")
      .text("Amplified Jet Stream (deep waves)");
    // Annotations
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 210).attr("y", 260).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).text("❄️ Cold trough");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 370).attr("y", 150).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).text("🔥 Warm ridge");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 530).attr("y", 280).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).text("❄️ Cold trough");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 330).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 13)
      .text("Deep waves → cold air plunges south, warm air pushes north → extreme weather STALLS");
  } else {
    svg.append("path")
      .attr("d", "M 50,195 Q 130,140 210,225 Q 290,300 370,180 Q 450,100 530,240 Q 610,310 700,190")
      .attr("stroke", "#e74c3c").attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-dasharray", "8,4");
    svg.append("path")
      .attr("d", "M 50,190 Q 200,170 350,195 Q 500,220 650,185 L 700,185")
      .attr("stroke", "#1565c0").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 80).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold").attr("fill", "#6c5ce7")
      .text("Climate Change → More Frequent Amplified Patterns?");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 200).attr("y", 155).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#1565c0").text("--- Historical pattern");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 200).attr("y", 175).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text("- - Future projection");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 375).attr("y", 330).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 13)
      .text("Arctic amplification may lead to more frequent blocking patterns → more extreme storms");
  }

  return svg.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Key Concept: The Jet Stream Steers Storms

- The **polar jet stream** is a band of fast-moving air (100–200+ mph) at ~30,000 ft altitude
- It forms at the boundary between cold polar and warm tropical air
- Mid-latitude storms **ride the jet stream** from west to east
- **Stronger temperature gradient** → faster, straighter jet → predictable storm tracks
- **Weaker gradient (Arctic amplification)** → slower, wavier jet → storms can **stall**, creating extended extreme events
:::

# Elaborate: Precipitation Patterns & Climate Connections

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🌧️ Where Does It Rain (and Snow)?

Global circulation doesn't just create wind patterns — it determines where on Earth gets rain and where stays dry.
:::

## Rising Air = Rain, Sinking Air = Dry

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
precipPatternData = [
  {lat: 0, name: "Equator (ITCZ)", precip: 2000, type: "Rising air → heavy rain", emoji: "🌧️"},
  {lat: 15, name: "15°N", precip: 1200, type: "Transition", emoji: "🌤️"},
  {lat: 30, name: "30°N (Horse latitudes)", precip: 300, type: "Sinking air → DESERTS", emoji: "🏜️"},
  {lat: 45, name: "45°N (Mid-latitudes)", precip: 1000, type: "Frontal lifting → moderate rain", emoji: "🌦️"},
  {lat: 60, name: "60°N (Polar front)", precip: 800, type: "Rising air → rain/snow", emoji: "🌨️"},
  {lat: 75, name: "75°N", precip: 250, type: "Cold sinking air → dry", emoji: "❄️"},
  {lat: 90, name: "90°N (Pole)", precip: 100, type: "Polar desert", emoji: "🧊"}
]

Plot.plot({
  title: "Average Annual Precipitation by Latitude",

  width: 700,

  ]
})
```

# Elaborate: Shifting Storm Paths

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🌡️ Could Climate Change Move Storm Tracks?

If the temperature gradient between the equator and poles changes, the circulation cells — and the jet stream — could shift. What would that mean for storms?
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof warmingScenario = Inputs.range([0, 4], {label: "Global warming (°C above pre-industrial)", step: 0.5, value: 0})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const width = 700;
  const height = 400;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);

  svg.append("rect").attr("width", width).attr("height", height).attr("fill", "#f8f9fa").attr("rx", 10);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 350).attr("y", 30).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 16).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text(`Storm Track Shift with ${warmingScenario}°C Warming`);

  // Latitude axis
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", 60).attr("y1", 360).attr("x2", 660).attr("y2", 360).attr("stroke", "#2d3436").attr("stroke-width", 2);
  const latLabels = ["20°N", "30°N", "40°N", "50°N", "60°N", "70°N"];
  latLabels.forEach((l, i) => {
    const x = 80 + i * 110;
    svg.append("text").attr("x", x).attr("y", 380).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).text(l);
  });

  // Current storm track density (bell curve around 40-45°N)
  const currentPeak = 300; // x position for 40°N
  const shift = warmingScenario * 25; // shift northward with warming

  // Historical curve
  const points = d3.range(80, 640, 5).map(x => {
    const y = 300 * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((x - currentPeak) / 100, 2));
    return {x, y};
  });

  svg.append("path")
    .attr("d", d3.line().x(d => d.x).y(d => 350 - d.y).curve(d3.curveBasis)(points))
    .attr("stroke", "#3498db").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("fill", "#3498db").attr("fill-opacity", 0.15)
    .attr("stroke-dasharray", warmingScenario > 0 ? "5,3" : "0");

  if (warmingScenario > 0) {
    // Shifted curve
    const shiftedPoints = d3.range(80, 640, 5).map(x => {
      const y = 280 * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((x - currentPeak - shift) / 120, 2));
      return {x, y};
    });

    svg.append("path")
      .attr("d", d3.line().x(d => d.x).y(d => 350 - d.y).curve(d3.curveBasis)(shiftedPoints))
      .attr("stroke", "#e74c3c").attr("stroke-width", 3).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").attr("fill-opacity", 0.2);
  }

  // NYC line
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", 310).attr("y1", 50).attr("x2", 310).attr("y2", 355).attr("stroke", "#2d3436").attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 310).attr("y", 45).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", "bold").text("NYC (41°N)");

  // Legend
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", 450).attr("y1", 70).attr("x2", 500).attr("y2", 70).attr("stroke", "#3498db").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("stroke-dasharray", warmingScenario > 0 ? "5,3" : "0");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 510).attr("y", 74).attr("font-size", 11).text("Historical track density");
  if (warmingScenario > 0) {
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", 450).attr("y1", 90).attr("x2", 500).attr("y2", 90).attr("stroke", "#e74c3c").attr("stroke-width", 3);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 510).attr("y", 94).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#e74c3c").text(`Projected (+${warmingScenario}°C)`);
  }

  // Impact note
  if (warmingScenario >= 2) {
    svg.append("rect").attr("x", 100).attr("y", 270).attr("width", 500).attr("height", 50).attr("fill", "#fff3e0").attr("rx", 8);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 350).attr("y", 293).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 13).attr("font-weight", "bold").attr("fill", "#e65100")
      .text("⚠️ Storm tracks shift poleward — NYC may see fewer but potentially stronger storms");
  }

  return svg.node();
}
```

::: {.mind-blown}
🌍 As the planet warms, the jet stream and storm tracks are projected to shift **poleward** — changing which regions get storms and how intense they are! 🌍
:::

# Elaborate: ENSO — The Pacific's Weather Remote Control

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🌊 El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO)

ENSO is a **cyclical shift in Pacific Ocean temperatures and wind patterns** that reorganizes storm tracks, precipitation, and hurricane activity across the entire planet. It is the single most powerful short-term driver of global weather variability — and climate change is making it more extreme.
:::

```{=html}
    <div id="enso-step-header">
      <div id="enso-step-title">🔬 Step-by-step Mechanism</div>
      <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;">
        <div id="enso-step-progress"></div>
        <div id="enso-step-btns">
          <button class="esb" id="esb-prev">← Prev</button>
          <button class="esb" id="esb-next">Next →</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div id="enso-steps-viewport" style="overflow:hidden;position:relative;">
      <div id="enso-steps"></div>
    </div>
    <div id="enso-step-dots"></div>
  </div>

</div>

<script>
(function(){
  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     DATA
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  const PHASES = {
    neutral: {
      emoji: '🌊',
      title: 'Neutral / Normal Conditions',
      sub: 'Trade winds blow west along the equator, piling warm water in the western Pacific near Indonesia. Cold, nutrient-rich water upwells off Peru. The Walker Circulation runs at normal strength.',
      oni: 'ONI: −0.4 to +0.4°C',
      btnGrad: 'linear-gradient(135deg,#4facfe,#00f2fe)',
      bannerGrad: 'linear-gradient(135deg,#0277bd,#0288d1)',
      warmPool: 0.5,       // 0=far west, 1=far east
      thermoclineAngle: 0, // degrees
      windStrength: 0.7,
      impacts: [
        {region:'Western Pacific',icon:'🌧️',label:'Normal Rainfall',desc:'Indonesia & Australia receive typical monsoon rainfall.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'Eastern Pacific',icon:'🐟',label:'Strong Upwelling',desc:'Cold nutrient-rich water supports large fish populations off Peru.',cls:'ei-cool'},
        {region:'Atlantic Basin',icon:'🌀',label:'Average Hurricane Season',desc:'Atlantic wind shear is at typical levels — moderate season expected.',cls:'ei-storm'},
        {region:'North America',icon:'🌤️',label:'Near-Normal Winters',desc:'Jet stream follows a typical path; precipitation near average.',cls:'ei-calm'},
        {region:'East Africa',icon:'🌦️',label:'Average Rainfall',desc:'East Africa receives near-normal seasonal precipitation.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'South Asia',icon:'🌧️',label:'Normal Monsoon',desc:'Indian Ocean monsoon tracks its typical seasonal pattern.',cls:'ei-wet'},
      ],
      steps: [
        {n:'1',name:'Trade Winds Blow West',body:'Normally, <strong>easterly trade winds</strong> blow from South America toward Asia along the equatorial Pacific. This wind is driven by the temperature difference between warm western and cool eastern Pacific.',note:'Key driver: Pressure difference between warm west Pacific and cool east Pacific.'},
        {n:'2',name:'Warm Water Pools in the West',body:'The trade winds push warm surface water westward, causing it to "pile up" near Indonesia and Australia. The western Pacific warm pool reaches temperatures of <strong>28–30°C</strong>.',note:'The warm pool can be up to 60 cm higher than the eastern Pacific surface.'},
        {n:'3',name:'Cold Upwelling Off Peru',body:'As warm surface water moves west, cold water from the deep ocean <strong>upwells</strong> along the coast of South America, keeping the eastern Pacific cool and nutrient-rich.',note:'Peru\'s anchovy fishery — one of the world\'s largest — depends on this upwelling.'},
        {n:'4',name:'The Walker Circulation',body:'Rising air over the warm western Pacific, westward flow aloft, sinking air over the cool eastern Pacific, and surface trade winds back west — this loop is called the <strong>Walker Circulation</strong>.',note:'George Walker first described this system in 1924 while studying Indian monsoon failures.'},
        {n:'5',name:'Teleconnections',body:'The Walker Circulation links weather patterns around the globe. The pressure difference between Darwin, Australia and Tahiti (the <strong>Southern Oscillation Index</strong>) measures this system\'s strength.',note:'A high SOI = La Niña conditions; a low SOI = El Niño conditions.'},
      ]
    },
    elnino: {
      emoji: '🔴',
      title: 'El Niño — The Warm Phase',
      sub: 'Trade winds weaken or reverse. Warm water surges east across the Pacific. Sea surface temperatures off Peru rise 0.5–3°C or more above normal, disrupting global weather patterns.',
      oni: 'ONI: ≥ +0.5°C (Strong: ≥ +1.5°C)',
      btnGrad: 'linear-gradient(135deg,#ef4444,#f97316)',
      bannerGrad: 'linear-gradient(135deg,#b71c1c,#e53935)',
      warmPool: 0.82,
      thermoclineAngle: 8,
      windStrength: 0.2,
      impacts: [
        {region:'Western Pacific',icon:'🌵',label:'Drought & Wildfires',desc:'Indonesia, Australia & Philippines suffer severe drought. 2015–16 saw massive peatland fires across Borneo.',cls:'ei-dry'},
        {region:'Eastern Pacific',icon:'🌡️',label:'Warm Sea Surface',desc:'Sea surface temperatures off Peru rise 2–4°C, killing fish and disrupting the entire food web.',cls:'ei-warm'},
        {region:'Atlantic Basin',icon:'😌',label:'Suppressed Hurricanes',desc:'Increased upper-level wind shear over the Atlantic inhibits hurricane formation. Fewer/weaker Atlantic storms.',cls:'ei-calm'},
        {region:'Southern U.S.',icon:'💧',label:'Wetter / Flooding',desc:'Southern tier from California to Florida sees above-normal winter rainfall. 1997–98: California floods.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'Northern U.S. / Canada',icon:'☀️',label:'Warmer/Drier Winters',desc:'The northern tier experiences mild, dry winters. Great Lakes ice cover is reduced dramatically.',cls:'ei-dry'},
        {region:'South America',icon:'🌊',label:'Coastal Flooding & Fish Die-off',desc:'Peru and Ecuador face catastrophic flooding; collapse of the anchovy fishery. Named "El Niño" by Peruvian fishermen.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'East Africa',icon:'🌧️',label:'Heavy Rains & Flooding',desc:'East Africa (Kenya, Somalia, Ethiopia) receives well-above-normal rainfall. 2019–20 saw massive flooding.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'South Asia',icon:'☁️',label:'Weakened Monsoon',desc:'India and Southeast Asia receive below-normal monsoon rainfall, risking drought and agricultural failure.',cls:'ei-dry'},
      ],
      steps: [
        {n:'1',name:'Trade Winds Weaken',body:'Every 2–7 years, the trade winds weaken — sometimes triggered by a burst of westerly winds. Without the eastward push from trade winds, warm water begins to slosh back east.',note:'The exact trigger is still actively researched. Westerly wind bursts in the western Pacific are key initiators.'},
        {n:'2',name:'Warm Water Surges Eastward',body:'A downwelling Kelvin wave — an ocean wave that travels at the thermocline level — propagates eastward at 2–3 m/s, carrying warm water across the entire Pacific basin in 2–3 months.',note:'Kelvin waves are trapped to the equator by Earth\'s rotation — they can only travel east along the equator.'},
        {n:'3',name:'Eastern Pacific Warms',body:'When the Kelvin wave arrives off South America, it deepens the thermocline and <strong>suppresses upwelling</strong>. Sea surface temperatures rise 0.5–3°C above normal, sometimes much more.',note:'1997–98 El Niño SST anomalies reached +5°C in some areas — the strongest ever recorded at that time.'},
        {n:'4',name:'Walker Circulation Reverses',body:'With warm water now in the east, convection (rising air) shifts eastward too. The Walker Circulation slows or reverses, fundamentally reorganizing global atmospheric pressure patterns.',note:'The Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) drops sharply negative during El Niño events.'},
        {n:'5',name:'Global Teleconnections Activate',body:'The shifted convection alters the jet stream globally through <strong>Rossby waves</strong>. These atmospheric waves propagate poleward, changing storm tracks across North America, Africa, South Asia, and beyond.',note:'El Niño events cost the global economy an estimated $35 billion on average and cause 23,000+ deaths per event.'},
        {n:'6',name:'Self-Limiting Feedback',body:'As warm water in the east cools (by releasing heat to the atmosphere) and the ocean adjusts, trade winds gradually recover. The system typically returns to neutral — or overshoots to La Niña.',note:'El Niño events typically last 9–12 months, peaking in boreal winter (Nov–Jan).'},
      ]
    },
    lanina: {
      emoji: '🔵',
      title: 'La Niña — The Cool Phase',
      sub: 'Trade winds strengthen beyond normal, pushing even more warm water west. The eastern Pacific cools below average. La Niña is essentially an amplified version of normal conditions.',
      oni: 'ONI: ≤ −0.5°C (Strong: ≤ −1.5°C)',
      btnGrad: 'linear-gradient(135deg,#2563eb,#06b6d4)',
      bannerGrad: 'linear-gradient(135deg,#1565c0,#0288d1)',
      warmPool: 0.18,
      thermoclineAngle: -9,
      windStrength: 1.0,
      impacts: [
        {region:'Western Pacific',icon:'🌊',label:'Enhanced Rainfall / Flooding',desc:'Indonesia, Philippines, and Australia see above-normal rainfall. 2010–11 La Niña caused Queensland\'s worst floods.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'Eastern Pacific',icon:'🧊',label:'Enhanced Upwelling',desc:'Stronger trade winds intensify cold water upwelling off Peru, benefiting fisheries but dropping SSTs.',cls:'ei-cool'},
        {region:'Atlantic Basin',icon:'🌀',label:'More Active Hurricane Season',desc:'Reduced upper-level wind shear favors hurricane development. 2010 La Niña produced 19 named storms.',cls:'ei-storm'},
        {region:'Southern U.S.',icon:'☀️',label:'Drought & Wildfires',desc:'Southern California, Texas, and the Gulf States tend to be drier than normal. Texas 2011 drought was La Niña–driven.',cls:'ei-dry'},
        {region:'Pacific Northwest / Great Plains',icon:'🌧️',label:'Wetter / Cooler Winters',desc:'The northern tier of the U.S. and Canada see increased snowpack and precipitation.',cls:'ei-wet'},
        {region:'South America',icon:'🌵',label:'Drought in SE South America',desc:'Argentina, Uruguay, and southern Brazil experience below-normal rainfall and agricultural stress.',cls:'ei-dry'},
        {region:'East Africa',icon:'☁️',label:'Below-Normal Rainfall',desc:'East Africa tends to be drier during La Niña, increasing drought and food insecurity risk.',cls:'ei-dry'},
        {region:'South Asia',icon:'🌧️',label:'Enhanced Monsoon',desc:'India and Southeast Asia receive above-normal monsoon rainfall, with flooding risks in some areas.',cls:'ei-wet'},
      ],
      steps: [
        {n:'1',name:'Strengthened Trade Winds',body:'After an El Niño, or independently, the trade winds intensify beyond their normal strength. This is often a rebound from the El Niño phase — the ocean and atmosphere overcorrect.',note:'The transition from El Niño to La Niña typically occurs within 6–12 months.'},
        {n:'2',name:'Warm Water Piles Up Even More in the West',body:'Stronger trades push even more warm water toward Indonesia and Australia, making the western Pacific warm pool deeper and warmer than normal.',note:'Sea level in the western Pacific can be 15–20 cm higher than the eastern Pacific during strong La Niña.'},
        {n:'3',name:'Enhanced Upwelling in the East',body:'The stronger wind stress on the ocean surface intensifies upwelling along South America, dragging even colder, deeper water to the surface than during neutral conditions.',note:'The thermocline (boundary between warm surface and cold deep water) tilts strongly — shallow in the east, deep in the west.'},
        {n:'4',name:'Walker Circulation Accelerates',body:'With enhanced east-west temperature contrast, the Walker Circulation strengthens — rising air over the western Pacific intensifies, driving stronger convection and more rainfall over Indonesia and Australia.',note:'SOI rises sharply positive during La Niña, indicating lower pressure at Darwin vs. Tahiti.'},
        {n:'5',name:'Atlantic Hurricane Enhancement',body:'A stronger Walker Circulation reduces upper-level winds over the Atlantic (less wind shear), creating favorable conditions for hurricane formation and intensification.',note:'La Niña years account for a disproportionate share of catastrophic Atlantic hurricane seasons.'},
        {n:'6',name:'Global Weather Reorganized',body:'Like El Niño but mirrored: dry where El Niño is wet, wet where El Niño is dry. North America\'s storm track shifts northward, bringing drought to the South and storms to the Pacific Northwest.',note:'La Niña events can last 1–3 years — often longer than El Niño events.'},
      ]
    }
  };

  /* ─── Historical ONI data (simplified annual averages, representative values) ─── */
  const ONI_DATA = [
    // [year, ONI anomaly]
    [1950,-1.4],[1951,0.7],[1952,0.1],[1953,0.5],[1954,-1.2],[1955,-1.6],
    [1956,-0.8],[1957,1.2],[1958,0.7],[1959,0.1],[1960,-0.4],[1961,-0.0],
    [1962,-0.4],[1963,0.7],[1964,-0.9],[1965,1.3],[1966,0.1],[1967,-0.5],
    [1968,0.7],[1969,0.9],[1970,-1.0],[1971,-1.3],[1972,1.8],[1973,-1.8],
    [1974,-1.1],[1975,-1.3],[1976,0.8],[1977,0.6],[1978,0.0],[1979,0.2],
    [1980,0.5],[1981,0.4],[1982,2.0],[1983,1.1],[1984,-0.6],[1985,-0.9],
    [1986,1.2],[1987,1.6],[1988,-1.7],[1989,-0.8],[1990,0.4],[1991,0.8],
    [1992,0.6],[1993,0.4],[1994,0.6],[1995,-0.7],[1996,-0.5],[1997,2.4],
    [1998,-1.4],[1999,-1.2],[2000,-0.8],[2001,-0.1],[2002,1.0],[2003,0.5],
    [2004,0.6],[2005,-0.5],[2006,0.8],[2007,-1.3],[2008,-0.8],[2009,1.0],
    [2010,-1.4],[2011,-1.2],[2012,0.2],[2013,-0.4],[2014,0.3],[2015,2.3],
    [2016,0.4],[2017,-0.8],[2018,0.9],[2019,-0.6],[2020,-1.3],[2021,-1.0],
    [2022,-0.9],[2023,1.9],[2024,0.2],[2025,-0.6]
  ];

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     STATE
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  let currentPhase = 'neutral';
  let currentStep = 0;
  let intensity = 60;
  let animFrame = null;
  let waveOffset = 0;

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     HELPERS
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  function lerp(a,b,t){ return a+(b-a)*t; }
  function clamp(v,lo,hi){ return Math.max(lo,Math.min(hi,v)); }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     CANVAS: Pacific Cross-Section
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  const canvas = document.getElementById('enso-canvas');
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

  function resizeCanvas(){
    const w = canvas.parentElement.offsetWidth;
    canvas.width = w;
    canvas.height = 240;
  }

  function drawPacific(){
    resizeCanvas();
    const p = PHASES[currentPhase];
    const W = canvas.width, H = canvas.height;
    const t = intensity/100;

    // Background ocean gradient
    const oceanGrad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,0,H);
    oceanGrad.addColorStop(0,'#0c2a4a');
    oceanGrad.addColorStop(1,'#041628');
    ctx.fillStyle = oceanGrad;
    ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);

    // Land masses
    function drawLand(x,w,label){
      const lg = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,0,H*0.22);
      lg.addColorStop(0,'#2d5a27');
      lg.addColorStop(1,'#1a3a16');
      ctx.fillStyle = lg;
      ctx.fillRect(x,0,w,H*0.22);
      ctx.fillStyle = '#a8d5a2';
      ctx.font = `bold ${Math.max(10,W*0.018)}px Inter,sans-serif`;
      ctx.textAlign = 'center';
      ctx.fillText(label, x+w/2, H*0.12);
    }
    drawLand(0, W*0.12, 'INDONESIA');
    drawLand(W*0.88, W*0.12, 'PERU');

    // Warm pool — position varies by phase + intensity
    const poolX = lerp(W*0.12, W*0.85, lerp(p.warmPool*0.6, p.warmPool, t));
    const poolW = W * lerp(0.3, 0.5, t);

    // Sea surface temperature color gradient
    for(let x=W*0.12; x<W*0.88; x+=2){
      const frac = (x - W*0.12)/(W*0.76);
      // Distance from warm pool center
      const distFromPool = Math.abs(x - poolX)/poolW;
      const warmth = clamp(1 - distFromPool, 0, 1);
      const temp = lerp(15, 30, warmth);
      const r = Math.round(lerp(0, 255, warmth));
      const g = Math.round(lerp(120, 180, 1-warmth*0.5));
      const b = Math.round(lerp(200, 50, warmth));
      ctx.fillStyle = `rgb(${r},${g},${b})`;
      ctx.fillRect(x, H*0.22, 2, H*0.12);
    }

    // Thermocline (dashed line — tilted by phase)
    const tcAngle = p.thermoclineAngle * t * Math.PI/180;
    const tcMidY = H * 0.55;
    ctx.setLineDash([8,5]);
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(0,200,255,0.7)';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath();
    const tcWest = tcMidY - Math.sin(tcAngle)*(W*0.38);
    const tcEast = tcMidY + Math.sin(tcAngle)*(W*0.38);
    ctx.moveTo(W*0.12, tcWest);
    ctx.lineTo(W*0.88, tcEast);
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);

    // Thermocline label
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,200,255,0.9)';
    ctx.font = `${Math.max(9,W*0.012)}px Inter,sans-serif`;
    ctx.textAlign = 'left';
    ctx.fillText('thermocline', W*0.14, tcWest - 6);

    // Deep cold water below thermocline
    const coldGrad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, tcMidY, 0, H);
    coldGrad.addColorStop(0,'rgba(0,100,180,0.3)');
    coldGrad.addColorStop(1,'rgba(0,30,80,0.5)');
    ctx.fillStyle = coldGrad;
    ctx.fillRect(W*0.12, tcMidY+4, W*0.76, H - tcMidY - 4);

    // Upwelling arrow (east coast) — stronger in La Niña, suppressed in El Niño
    const upwellStrength = currentPhase==='elnino' ? (1-t)*0.4 : currentPhase==='lanina' ? 0.5+t*0.5 : 0.5;
    if(upwellStrength > 0.1){
      const ux = W*0.84;
      const arrowH = H*0.18*upwellStrength;
      ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(0,210,230,${upwellStrength*0.9})`;
      ctx.lineWidth = 2.5;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(ux, H*0.55);
      ctx.lineTo(ux, H*0.55 - arrowH);
      ctx.stroke();
      // arrowhead
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(ux, H*0.55 - arrowH);
      ctx.lineTo(ux-6, H*0.55 - arrowH + 10);
      ctx.lineTo(ux+6, H*0.55 - arrowH + 10);
      ctx.closePath();
      ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(0,210,230,${upwellStrength*0.9})`;
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,210,230,0.8)';
      ctx.font = `${Math.max(8,W*0.012)}px Inter,sans-serif`;
      ctx.textAlign = 'center';
      ctx.fillText('upwelling', ux, H*0.55 - arrowH - 6);
    }

    // Animated trade wind arrows
    const ws = p.windStrength * t * 0.7 + p.windStrength * 0.3;
    const numArrows = 5;
    const arrowY = H * 0.16;
    for(let i=0;i<numArrows;i++){
      const baseX = W*0.15 + (W*0.7/numArrows)*i;
      const offset = ((waveOffset * (currentPhase==='elnino'?-1:1)) % (W*0.7/numArrows));
      const ax = (baseX + offset + W*0.76) % (W*0.76) + W*0.12;
      const len = 30 * ws;
      const dir = currentPhase==='elnino' && t>0.5 ? 1 : -1; // reverse in strong El Niño
      ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(255,255,200,${ws*0.8})`;
      ctx.lineWidth = 2;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(ax, arrowY);
      ctx.lineTo(ax + dir*len, arrowY);
      ctx.stroke();
      // arrowhead
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(ax + dir*len, arrowY);
      ctx.lineTo(ax + dir*len - dir*8, arrowY - 5);
      ctx.lineTo(ax + dir*len - dir*8, arrowY + 5);
      ctx.closePath();
      ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(255,255,200,${ws*0.8})`;
      ctx.fill();
    }

    // Wind label
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,200,0.9)';
    ctx.font = `bold ${Math.max(9,W*0.012)}px Inter,sans-serif`;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    const windLabel = currentPhase==='elnino' && t>0.6 ? '← Reversed/Weak Trades' : '← Trade Winds (Easterlies)';
    ctx.fillText(windLabel, W*0.5, arrowY - 12);

    // Warm pool / SST label
    const sst = currentPhase==='elnino' ? (28+t*2.5).toFixed(1) : currentPhase==='lanina' ? (28-t*1.5).toFixed(1) : '28.5';
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,160,80,0.95)';
    ctx.font = `bold ${Math.max(10,W*0.014)}px Inter,sans-serif`;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.fillText(`🌡️ ${sst}°C`, poolX, H*0.36);

    // Phase label overlay
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.12)';
    ctx.fillRect(W*0.12, H*0.88, W*0.76, H*0.1);
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.7)';
    ctx.font = `${Math.max(10,W*0.013)}px Inter,sans-serif`;
    ctx.textAlign = 'left';
    ctx.fillText('🌏 West (Warm)', W*0.15, H*0.95);
    ctx.textAlign = 'right';
    ctx.fillText('East (Cold/Upwelling) 🌎', W*0.85, H*0.95);
  }

  function animLoop(){
    waveOffset = (waveOffset + 0.8) % 1000;
    drawPacific();
    animFrame = requestAnimationFrame(animLoop);
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     IMPACT CARDS
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  function renderImpacts(){
    const p = PHASES[currentPhase];
    const container = document.getElementById('enso-impacts');
    container.innerHTML = p.impacts.map(imp=>`
      <div class="ei-card ${imp.cls}">
        <div class="ei-region">${imp.region}</div>
        <div class="ei-icon">${imp.icon}</div>
        <div class="ei-label">${imp.label}</div>
        <div class="ei-desc">${imp.desc}</div>
      </div>`).join('');
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     BANNER
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  function renderBanner(){
    const p = PHASES[currentPhase];
    const banner = document.getElementById('enso-banner');
    banner.style.background = p.bannerGrad;
    document.getElementById('enso-banner-emoji').textContent = p.emoji;
    document.getElementById('enso-banner-title').textContent = p.title;
    document.getElementById('enso-banner-sub').textContent = p.sub;
    document.getElementById('enso-oni').textContent = p.oni;
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     STEPPER
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  function renderStepper(){
    const steps = PHASES[currentPhase].steps;
    const container = document.getElementById('enso-steps');
    container.style.display = 'flex';
    container.style.transition = 'transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)';
    container.innerHTML = steps.map((s,i)=>`
      <div class="enso-step" style="min-width:100%;box-sizing:border-box;">
        <span class="es-num">${s.n}</span><span class="es-name">${s.name}</span>
        <div class="es-body">${s.body}</div>
        <div class="es-note">${s.note}</div>
      </div>`).join('');
    // dots
    const dots = document.getElementById('enso-step-dots');
    dots.innerHTML = steps.map((_,i)=>`<div class="esd ${i===currentStep?'esd-active':''}"></div>`).join('');
    updateStepView();
  }

  function updateStepView(){
    const steps = PHASES[currentPhase].steps;
    document.getElementById('enso-steps').style.transform = `translateX(-${currentStep*100}%)`;
    document.querySelectorAll('.esd').forEach((d,i)=>{
      d.classList.toggle('esd-active', i===currentStep);
    });
    document.getElementById('enso-step-progress').textContent = `${currentStep+1} / ${steps.length}`;
  }

  document.getElementById('esb-next').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const n = PHASES[currentPhase].steps.length;
    currentStep = (currentStep+1) % n;
    updateStepView();
  });
  document.getElementById('esb-prev').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const n = PHASES[currentPhase].steps.length;
    currentStep = (currentStep-1+n) % n;
    updateStepView();
  });

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     HISTORICAL ONI CHART
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  const chartCanvas = document.getElementById('enso-chart');
  const cctx = chartCanvas.getContext('2d');

  function drawOniChart(){
    const W = chartCanvas.parentElement.offsetWidth - 36;
    chartCanvas.width = W;
    chartCanvas.height = 110;
    const CH = chartCanvas.height;
    const PAD = {l:36, r:10, t:10, b:20};
    const dW = (W-PAD.l-PAD.r) / ONI_DATA.length;
    const maxV = 2.6;

    cctx.clearRect(0,0,W,CH);

    // Zero line
    const zeroY = PAD.t + (CH-PAD.t-PAD.b)/2;
    cctx.strokeStyle = '#cbd5e0';
    cctx.lineWidth = 1;
    cctx.setLineDash([4,3]);
    cctx.beginPath();
    cctx.moveTo(PAD.l,zeroY);
    cctx.lineTo(W-PAD.r,zeroY);
    cctx.stroke();
    cctx.setLineDash([]);

    // ±0.5 threshold lines
    [0.5,-0.5].forEach(v=>{
      const y = zeroY - v*((CH-PAD.t-PAD.b)/2)/maxV;
      cctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(150,150,150,0.35)';
      cctx.lineWidth = 1;
      cctx.setLineDash([2,4]);
      cctx.beginPath();
      cctx.moveTo(PAD.l,y); cctx.lineTo(W-PAD.r,y);
      cctx.stroke();
      cctx.setLineDash([]);
    });

    // Bars
    ONI_DATA.forEach(([yr,v],i)=>{
      const x = PAD.l + i*dW;
      const barH = Math.abs(v)*(CH-PAD.t-PAD.b)/2/maxV;
      const y = v>=0 ? zeroY-barH : zeroY;
      const isNino = v >= 0.5;
      const isNina = v <= -0.5;
      cctx.fillStyle = isNino ? `rgba(239,68,68,0.85)` : isNina ? `rgba(37,99,235,0.85)` : 'rgba(150,150,150,0.55)';
      cctx.fillRect(x, y, Math.max(dW-1,1), barH);
    });

    // Y labels
    cctx.fillStyle = '#718096';
    cctx.font = '9px Inter,sans-serif';
    cctx.textAlign = 'right';
    [2,1,0,-1,-2].forEach(v=>{
      const y = zeroY - v*(CH-PAD.t-PAD.b)/2/maxV;
      cctx.fillText(v===0?'0':v>0?`+${v}`:v, PAD.l-3, y+3);
    });

    // X labels (every 10 years)
    cctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ONI_DATA.forEach(([yr,v],i)=>{
      if(yr%10===0){
        const x = PAD.l + i*dW + dW/2;
        cctx.fillText(yr, x, CH-4);
      }
    });

    // Legend
    cctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(239,68,68,0.85)';
    cctx.fillRect(PAD.l,4,10,8);
    cctx.fillStyle = '#4a5568'; cctx.font='9px Inter,sans-serif'; cctx.textAlign='left';
    cctx.fillText('El Niño',PAD.l+13,11);
    cctx.fillStyle='rgba(37,99,235,0.85)';
    cctx.fillRect(PAD.l+52,4,10,8);
    cctx.fillStyle='#4a5568';
    cctx.fillText('La Niña',PAD.l+65,11);
  }

  // Click on chart to highlight a year
  chartCanvas.addEventListener('click', e=>{
    const rect = chartCanvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    const x = (e.clientX - rect.left) * (chartCanvas.width/rect.width);
    const PAD_L = 36, dW = (chartCanvas.width-46)/ONI_DATA.length;
    const idx = Math.floor((x-PAD_L)/dW);
    if(idx>=0 && idx<ONI_DATA.length){
      const [yr,v] = ONI_DATA[idx];
      const phase = v>=0.5?'elnino':v<=-0.5?'lanina':'neutral';
      setPhase(phase);
      // show year tooltip briefly
      const tip = document.createElement('div');
      tip.style.cssText='position:fixed;background:#2d3748;color:white;padding:5px 10px;border-radius:8px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;pointer-events:none;z-index:9999;transition:opacity 0.4s;';
      tip.textContent = `${yr}: ONI = ${v>0?'+':''}${v}°C`;
      document.body.appendChild(tip);
      const cr = chartCanvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      tip.style.left = (cr.left + x*(cr.width/chartCanvas.width) - 40)+'px';
      tip.style.top = (cr.top - 36)+'px';
      setTimeout(()=>{ tip.style.opacity='0'; setTimeout(()=>tip.remove(),400); }, 1800);
    }
  });

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     PHASE CHANGE
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  function setPhase(phase){
    currentPhase = phase;
    currentStep = 0;
    // Update buttons
    document.querySelectorAll('.enso-btn').forEach(b=>{
      const active = b.dataset.phase === phase;
      b.classList.toggle('ep-active', active);
      if(active){
        b.style.background = PHASES[phase].btnGrad;
        b.style.borderColor = 'transparent';
        b.style.color = 'white';
      } else {
        b.style.background = '#f7fafc';
        b.style.borderColor = '#cbd5e0';
        b.style.color = '#4a5568';
      }
    });
    renderBanner();
    renderImpacts();
    renderStepper();
  }

  document.querySelectorAll('.enso-btn').forEach(b=>{
    b.addEventListener('click',()=>setPhase(b.dataset.phase));
  });

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     INTENSITY SLIDER
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  const slider = document.getElementById('enso-intensity');
  const sliderLabel = document.getElementById('enso-intensity-label');
  slider.addEventListener('input',()=>{
    intensity = +slider.value;
    const labels = ['Weak','Weak-Moderate','Moderate','Strong','Very Strong'];
    sliderLabel.textContent = labels[Math.floor(intensity/20)] || 'Very Strong';
  });

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
     INIT
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  setPhase('neutral');
  drawOniChart();
  animLoop();

  window.addEventListener('resize',()=>{
    drawPacific();
    drawOniChart();
  });

})();
</script>
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 🔑 Key Connections: ENSO and Storm Paths

- **El Niño → fewer Atlantic hurricanes** (increased wind shear) but **more Eastern Pacific hurricanes**
- **La Niña → more Atlantic hurricanes** (reduced wind shear) — 2005, 2010, 2020 seasons were all La Niña years
- **El Niño → southern U.S. jet stream dips south**, steering storms across the Gulf States into Florida
- **La Niña → jet stream shifts north**, routing storms across the Pacific Northwest and Great Plains
- ENSO cycles every **2–7 years** and account for ~30% of year-to-year weather variability
- Climate change is projected to make **extreme El Niño and La Niña events more frequent** as the Pacific Ocean warms
:::

# Summary: Key Takeaways

| Concept | Key Idea |
|---------|----------|
| **Uneven heating** | Equator gets more solar energy → drives convection cells |
| **Convection cells** | Hadley, Ferrel, Polar cells redistribute heat globally |
| **Coriolis effect** | Earth's rotation deflects winds → creates prevailing wind patterns |
| **Westerlies** | Dominant winds in 30°–60° latitude → steer storms SW → NE |
| **Jet stream** | Fast upper-level winds at cell boundaries → storm "highway" |
| **Arctic amplification** | Reduced gradient → wavier jet stream → storms may stall or shift |
| **Storm tracks** | Both hurricanes and blizzards are steered by the same global winds |

**Next up:** We'll investigate **how hurricanes form** and why they only occur during certain months. 🌀
